clue.text: After spring, linked together having friends in high places

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, so the spring comes first here

parts.note: a spring is a natural source of water, a well
things linked together are connected

explanation.surface: Someone who, after a spring of networking, is now linked up with people of influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-connected is the idiom for knowing influential or powerful people.

clue.text: Darkest day, maybe, with client stories condemned

indicators.note: condemned stories are wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer's gloomiest day, when the client's accounts are dismissed by the court.
explanation.walkthrough: W (with) leads, and 'condemned' rearranges CLIENTSTORIES to give the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The winter solstice has the shortest daylight of the year, so it is the darkest day; 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Village regularly supplying drink

indicators.note: the run of words supplies the answer from within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of village into the start of regularly

explanation.surface: A village that regularly provides a drink, perhaps from its pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like a signal to take alternate letters of village, which gives nothing useful; it is part of the text holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: Felix perhaps let out who's performing in exhibition

parts.note: Felix the Cat is a famous cartoon cat, so Felix is an example of a cat

indicators.note: let out suggests letters set loose and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: letters that are performing are acting up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A cat is let out of its basket to see who is performing at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: TLE comes from rearranging LET and SHOW from rearranging WHOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle show is an agricultural exhibition where livestock are displayed and judged.

clue.text: A river once more rises and falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
once more means again

explanation.surface: A river that keeps rising and falling, like a tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like the river's level dropping, but it is the definition, a famous waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls is the celebrated waterfall on the US-Canada border, so Niagara names those falls.

clue.text: Copse's last two trees? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the final letter of the word copse is the one taken

parts.note: the last letter of copse
the yew and the ash are two trees

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a copse ends with just two trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for talk meant to deceive, rubbish or humbug.

clue.text: Music-maker raised an objection

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: the indefinite article an gives A
a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: A musician spoke up to make an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass instrument, something that makes music.

clue.text: Something that might go to the head of a slow learner?

definitions.text: Something that might go to the head of a slow learner?

parts.words: Something that might go to the head of a slow learner?
parts.note: the conical hat once put on a dull pupil's head as punishment, with a play on things going to one's head

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to the head' suggests success making someone vain; here it is literal, a hat placed on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce's cap was the paper cone that schoolchildren judged slow were made to wear.

clue.text: Rude part, figuratively speaking

parts.note: vulgar means rude or coarse
a fraction is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: Someone speaks metaphorically about an indecent part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figuratively' reads as metaphorically, but it means in figures, in numbers, which is how the answer is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction such as three quarters is written in figures, numerator over denominator, so it is spoken of in figures.

clue.text: Dark horse's very unpleasant experience

parts.note: night means darkness, the dark
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: An outsider in a race has a terrible time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' reads as an unknown contender, but the words split into night and mare.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare, besides a bad dream, is any very distressing or frightening ordeal.

clue.text: African veto on leaders of trade union

indicators.note: in an across clue, the ban is placed on, before, the letters that follow

parts.note: to veto is to ban

indicators.note: the first letters, the leaders, of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: An African politician vetoes proposals from the heads of a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bantu are a large family of peoples of central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Record group of men roller-skating

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle men and roller

explanation.surface: Someone documents a group of men out roller-skating.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to enter a name on a register or list, so to record.

clue.text: A reduced ticket price is some way off

indicators.note: the word for the ticket price is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a fare is the price of a travel ticket

explanation.surface: A discounted ticket for a journey that is quite a distance away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced ticket price' looks like a discount, but it means the word fare with its end removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a distance, far away.

clue.text: Bird losing its tail, going back to find hill

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read backwards
the last letter of the bird's name is dropped

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail feathers retreats to look for a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: GREBE without its last letter is GREB, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg is a South African word for a mountain or hill, familiar from place names.

clue.text: Worker with ice I included put this in radiator

indicators.note: the I is included within the other letters, between the insect and the freezing

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
to ice something is to freeze it

explanation.surface: A worker mentions ice and is told to add something to the car's radiator.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is the liquid added to an engine's coolant in the radiator to stop it freezing.

clue.text: Possibly as new as somewhere in Wales

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Comparing a place to see whether it is as new as somewhere in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales.

clue.text: Impression of past brilliance, but not before sunset?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lingering pleasant memory of a past success
second meaning: the light in the sky after the sun has gone down

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the literal sense: the glow comes after, not before, the sun sets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the warm remembered feeling after a triumph and the literal glow remaining after sunset.

clue.text: Worry briefly after worker's tracked vehicle in America

indicators.note: the shortened worry comes after the worker

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand; the 's means has

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: A worker frets a little over a vehicle running on rails in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A handcar is a small hand-pumped railway car, an American term for a vehicle that runs on track.

clue.text: Disappointment with puncture?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is something that disappoints
second meaning: a tyre with a puncture has been ..., deflated

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a punctured tyre is literally let down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an anticlimax or disappointment, and also the deflating of a tyre.

clue.text: No ancient city is hard to feed

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: No ancient city finds it easy to feed its population.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to give food and sustenance to.

clue.text: Cry endlessly when framing one politician, Republican

indicators.note: the shortened word surrounds the next letters like a frame
the last letter of when is removed

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament
R is the US abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone sobs without end when a Republican politician is framed.
explanation.walkthrough: WHE is when without its last letter; it goes round I and MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimper is a low, feeble cry or whine.

clue.text: One striking something uncommonly large

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who whops, hits or beats
second meaning: something unusually big, like a whopping lie

explanation.definitionFit: To whop is to strike hard, and a whopper is also slang for anything enormous.

clue.text: Run back? That's wrong!

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: Someone told to run back protests that it is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong for which damages may be claimed.

clue.text: Half of referees love sport

indicators.note: the first half of the word is taken

parts.note: judges act as referees
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Half the referees adore a particular sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art practised as a combat sport.

clue.text: Piece of history made by student, one in park

indicators.note: the student and the one go inside the park

parts.note: rec, short for recreation ground, is a public park
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A student finds a historical artefact while sitting in a park.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British recreation ground, a local park.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, a fragment of history.

clue.text: Poorest field sat empty

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word

indicators.note: the word is emptied of its inside letters, keeping its ends

parts.note: first and last letters of sat

explanation.surface: The poorest field lay unused and empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Least means smallest or lowest in amount or quality, so the poorest.

clue.text: Old Peruvian elected czar, oddly

parts.note: a party elected to power is in

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

parts.note: the first and third letters of czar

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian elected as a czar, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were the people who ruled an empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Pass on stretch of canal?

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Asking someone to move along a stretch of waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway, but it is the alimentary canal of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the large intestine, a section of the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Showmen rearranged primaries

indicators.note: the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Showmen reorganised the order of the primary elections.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios, plural impresari, are organisers and promoters of shows and concerts.

clue.text: Lost to the elements?

parts.note: something defeated by wind and rain has been beaten by the weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' reads as missing, but it means beaten, and the elements are the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten describes something worn and damaged by long exposure to wind, rain and sun.
